content.text:
I asked the site and I'm holding back. The page says to hold the money at "פסגות ניירות ערך בע"מ" in a fund called "ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500". After 15 years I'd have about 179,889 ₪ "בכסף של היום". For that the page assumes prices rise 2% a year. I'm fairly sure that's what the page says, but I wouldn't do it before I talk to you. The 179,889 only comes true if the share market grows 7% every year. The page set that 7% itself, not me. It also adds "אם הדולר לא זז מול השקל", so the money is really in dollars.

**What I did:**
- **My plan:** I typed 0 ₪ at the start, 750 ₪ a month and 15 years into the boxes and left the 7% alone. It showed 135,000 ₪ put in and 179,889 ₪ at the end.
- **Inflation:** I pressed the "אינפלציה" button. A small window showed "אינפלציה בשנה" 2%, "בכמה המחירים עולים בשנה, בממוצע". I left it at 2 and closed it.
- **Where to hold it:** below that, the box marked "הזול" named Psagot and the Yelin Lapidot fund. Under the fund it says 0% and "0.02%". Psagot charges 2,604 ₪ over the 15 years.

**What I didn't understand:**
- "S&P", read letter by letter.
- "מדד" here isn't the price index I know from the news.
- "קרן מחקה", "דמי משמרת", "נאמן", "עסקת החלף", "צוברת", "מנוטרלת מט"ח" and "מחלקת דיבידנד". I skipped them all.
- The slider for the monthly amount showed 800 while my box said 750.

**What bothered me:**
- The screen is black, and the grey writing on it is hard to read even enlarged. That includes the line "הבחירה שלכם; האתר לא ממליץ על מדד" and the exchange-rate line.
- Next to the second choice there was a "−122 ₪", and minus signs make me nervous.
- The second screen is a long coloured bar full of numbers. The pink part says 15,364, which I think is the tax, but the colours are too close together to be sure.

That's where I got tired and stopped. I didn't read the long list of funds and buttons below.

input.answer: The page says to hold it in a Psagot (פסגות ניירות ערך) account in the "ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500" fund. It assumes 2% inflation a year, plus a 7% yearly return and a steady dollar, so I'd ask my son before doing it.
